Documentation.name: Eriksson-Penker Models
Documentation.notes: A set of stereotypes and tagged values for modeling business processes.

Stereotype.name: process
Stereotype.notes: A process is a description of a set of related activities that, when correctly performed, will satisfy a specific goal.

Tag.name: Goal
Tag.description: Describes the goal if not explicitly attached to the process.

Tag.name: Purpose
Tag.description: Informally describes the purpose of the process.

Tag.name: Owner
Tag.description: Defines the person who has overall responsibility for the process.

Tag.name: Actors
Tag.description: Defines the process actors and their skills if not explicitly attached to the process.

Tag.name: Risks
Tag.description: Describes the risks associated with the process.

Tag.name: Possibilities
Tag.description: Describes the potential in terms of opportunities.

Tag.name: Time
Tag.description: The approximate duration of the process.

Tag.name: Cost
Tag.description: The approximate cost of executing the process.

Stereotype.name: information
Stereotype.notes: Information resource.

Stereotype.name: resource
Stereotype.notes: Consumable resource used during process.

Stereotype.name: abstract
Stereotype.notes: Abstract resource.

Stereotype.name: people
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: physical
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: business event
Stereotype.notes: Business event as class or instance.

Stereotype.name: goal
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: object read
Stereotype.notes: An object from the assembly line to a process.

Stereotype.name: object written
Stereotype.notes: An object delivered from a Process to the assembly line.

Stereotype.name: process decision
Stereotype.notes: Decision point between processes.

Stereotype.name: business rule
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: problem
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: cause
Stereotype.notes: Shows the cause of the problem.

Stereotype.name: prerequisite
Stereotype.notes: Shows the prerequisites for the action.

Stereotype.name: process flow
Stereotype.notes: A process control.

Stereotype.name: decision flow
Stereotype.notes: A process control after a decision point.

Stereotype.name: resource flow
Stereotype.notes: Object flow that shows that an object is produced by one process and consumed by another.

Stereotype.name: input
Stereotype.notes: Object flow that shows that a resource is consumed by a process.

Stereotype.name: output
Stereotype.notes: Object flow that shows that a resource is produced by a process.

Stereotype.name: non-causal
Stereotype.notes: Shows an object may be produced by one process and consumed by another.

Stereotype.name: process control
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is controlled by an object.

Stereotype.name: achieve
Stereotype.notes: A goal connection.

Stereotype.name: supply
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: contradictory
Stereotype.notes: Shows a process is supplied by an object.

Stereotype.name: assembly line
Stereotype.notes: Synchronizes and supplies processes in terms of objects.
